title: TraceLite: Efficient Trace Reduction for SWE Agents via Optical Compression and Redundancy Removal
title_zh: TraceLite：通过光学压缩与冗余去除实现SWE智能体的高效轨迹精简

paragraphs.en: Software engineering agents solve repository-level tasks through iterative tool use, but their continuously growing interaction traces incur substantial token consumption and inference overhead. Existing compression approaches often require model training, auxiliary LLM calls, or assumptions about specific content such as source code. We present TraceLite, a simple yet effective, training-free framework for compressing heterogeneous SWE-agent observations. Our preliminary study shows that optical rendering preserves substantial textual and semantic information under moderate compression, while agent trajectories exhibit both cross-step and phase-level redundancy. Motivated by these findings, TraceLite preserves recent observations as high-fidelity text, renders historical observations as compact images, removes overlapping content, and discards phase-expired observation payloads after code editing. It requires neither offline training nor auxiliary LLM inference. We evaluate TraceLite on SWE-bench Verified and DeepSWE using GPT-5.6-Luna and Gemini-3.8-Flash as backbone models. On SWE-bench Verified, TraceLite achieves 78.25% resolve rate, outperforming the evaluated compression baselines while reducing average input-token consumption and API cost by 33.05% and 21.30%, respectively. Moreover, it introduces only 0.438 seconds of compression latency per observation. These results demonstrate that TraceLite improves SWE-agent efficiency with low processing overhead and without compromising issue-resolution capability. Our code is available at https://github.com/xjywhu/TraceLite .

paragraphs.en: Large language models have evolved from passive code-generation tools into coding agents that autonomously interact with software development environments ( Yang et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ) . Equipped with interfaces for repository search, file editing, command execution, and testing, these agents have been applied to tasks such as fault localization, program repair, test generation, and issue resolution. Rather than producing a solution in a single invocation, a coding agent iteratively inspects the repository, invokes tools, interprets their outputs, and adjusts its subsequent actions. SWE-agent exemplifies this paradigm by introducing an agent–computer interface through which an LLM can navigate repositories, modify files, and execute tests ( Yang et al., 2024 ) . Its evaluation on SWE-bench, a benchmark constructed from real-world GitHub issues, demonstrates the potential of agents to perform repository-level debugging and patch generation ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型已从被动的代码生成工具演变为能够自主与软件开发环境交互的智能体（Yang et al., 2024；Wang et al., 2024）。 这些智能体配备了用于仓库搜索、文件编辑、命令执行和测试的接口，已被应用于故障定位、程序修复、测试生成和问题解决等任务。 编码智能体并非通过单次调用就产生解决方案，而是迭代地检查仓库、调用工具、解读工具输出并调整其后续动作。 SWE-agent 通过引入一种智能体—计算机接口体现了这一范式，借助该接口，大语言模型可以在仓库中导航、修改文件并执行测试（Yang et al., 2024）。 该智能体在 SWE-bench（一个基于真实 GitHub 问题构建的基准）上的评估表明，智能体具有执行仓库级调试与补丁生成的潜力（Jimenez et al., 2024）。

paragraphs.en: However, this iterative workflow causes the interaction trajectory to grow continuously ( Xiao et al., 2026 ; Gao and Peng, 2026 ) . Tool observations such as source code, search results, command outputs, and test logs are repeatedly included in subsequent prompts. Retaining redundant, outdated, or irrelevant observations increases inference cost and context window pressure and may distract the model from evidence needed for its current decision. Effective context management is therefore essential for compressing historical interaction traces while preserving information useful for future actions.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，这种迭代式工作流会导致交互轨迹持续增长（Xiao 等，2026；Gao 和 Peng，2026）。 诸如源代码、搜索结果、命令输出和测试日志等工具观察结果会被反复包含在后续提示中。 保留冗余、过时或无关的观察结果会增加推理成本和上下文窗口压力，并可能使智能体的注意力偏离其当前决策所需的证据。 因此，有效的上下文管理对于压缩历史交互痕迹同时保留对未来行动有用的信息至关重要。

paragraphs.en: Existing context compression methods differ in their targets, redundancy criteria, and context-handling strategies, as summarized in Table 1 . LLMLingua2 ( Pan et al., 2024 ) learns token-level importance using a dedicated compressor, whereas LongCodeZip ( Shi et al., 2025 ) uses conditional perplexity to prune code at the function and block levels. SWE-Pruner ( Wang et al., 2026 ) instead employs a trained neural pruner to perform line-level code filtering. SeeRepo ( Ma et al., 2026a ) constructs and renders repository graphs to guide code exploration, augmenting the agent’s context rather than compressing its accumulated trajectory. AgentDiet ( Xiao et al., 2026 ) directly reduces agent trajectories, but relies on an auxiliary reflection LLM to identify and remove redundant or expired information. Consequently, existing approaches require either learned components, auxiliary model inference, or repository-specific preprocessing, and do not provide a training-free and auxiliary-free solution for context compressing.
paragraphs.zh: 现有的上下文压缩方法在目标、冗余标准和上下文处理策略上各不相同，如表1所示。 LLMLingua2（Pan et al., 2024）使用专门的压缩器学习词元级别的重要性，而 LongCodeZip（Shi et al., 2025）则利用条件困惑度在函数和代码块级别对代码进行剪枝。 SWE-Pruner（Wang et al., 2026）则采用训练好的神经剪枝器来执行行级别的代码过滤。 SeeRepo（Ma et al., 2026a）构建并渲染仓库图以引导代码探索，是对智能体上下文的增强而非对其累积轨迹的压缩。 AgentDiet（Xiao et al., 2026）直接缩减智能体轨迹，但依赖一个辅助的反思 LLM 来识别并移除冗余或过期的信息。 因此，现有方法要么需要经过学习的组件，要么需要辅助模型推理，要么需要针对仓库的预处理，无法提供一种免训练且免辅助的上下文压缩解决方案。

paragraphs.en: These limitations raise a natural question: can interaction traces be compressed effectively without training a dedicated compressor or invoking an auxiliary model? Answering this question requires examining two complementary aspects of an agent trajectory: representation and content . First, can verbose observations be represented more compactly while preserving the information required by the agent? Second, does every observation remain necessary throughout the entire issue-resolution process?

paragraphs.en: To answer these questions, we conduct a preliminary study of SWE-agent trajectories. Regarding representation, we find that rendering observations as images preserves substantial character-level and semantic information under moderate compression. However, rendering the entire trajectory degrades issue-resolution performance because recent observations often contain precise evidence needed for the next action. Regarding content, we identify two forms of redundancy. First, observations from different interaction steps exhibit substantial textual overlap. Second, localization and diagnostic observations become largely unnecessary after the agent applies a concrete code modification, as their information has been incorporated into the updated repository state. These findings motivate a hybrid strategy that preserves recent evidence, compresses historical observations, and removes redundant content.

paragraphs.en: Motivated by these findings, we propose TraceLite, a simple yet effective training-free framework for compressing SWE-agent interaction traces. TraceLite divides the trajectory into recent and historical windows: recent observations are retained as high-fidelity text, while observations leaving the recent window are rendered as compact images. Within the recent window, TraceLite detects textual overlap and removes duplicated content from earlier observations while preserving their tool calls and non-overlapping information. Moreover, when the agent performs a code-editing action, TraceLite treats the edit as a phase transition and clears the preceding observation payloads while keeping the historical tool-call sequence. The complete procedure requires neither model training nor auxiliary LLM calls and supports heterogeneous tool observations.

paragraphs.en: Our contributions are summarized as follows:

paragraphs.en: We conduct a preliminary study of SWE-agent trajectories and identify three opportunities for compression: optical rendering preserves substantial information under moderate compression, observations across different steps contain considerable textual overlap, and pre-edit observations become largely unnecessary after the repository is modified.

paragraphs.en: We propose TraceLite, a simple yet effective trace-compression framework that combines historical optical compression and redundancy removal. It requires neither model training nor auxiliary LLM calls and supports heterogeneous tool observations.

paragraphs.en: Before presenting the design of TraceLite, we conduct a preliminary study to examine two properties of SWE-agent interaction traces. First, we investigate whether historical observations can be represented more compactly without losing their textual details or task-relevant semantics. Second, we examine whether observations produced at different interaction steps contain redundant or overlapping information. These two questions motivate the optical compression and trajectory refinement components of TraceLite, respectively. We collect interaction trajectories generated by GPT-5.6-Luna ( OpenAI, 2026b ) using the mini-SWE-agent ( Yang et al., 2024 ) framework on SWE-bench Verified ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) .

paragraphs.en: Recent OCR-based context compression methods ( Wei et al., 2025 ; Shi et al., 2026 ) demonstrate that visually rendered text can be represented using fewer tokens than its original textual form. Inspired by this observation, we consider rendering historical SWE-agent observations as images. However, software engineering observations require fidelity at both the character and semantic levels. At the character level, the agent must accurately recognize file paths, identifiers, line numbers, and error messages. At the semantic level, it must understand information such as program behavior, the purpose of a code fragment, and the cause of a test failure. Even a minor recognition error or semantic distortion may mislead subsequent agent decisions. We therefore investigate whether optical rendering preserves both the textual details and task-relevant semantics of agent observations.

paragraphs.en: (2) Semantic question answering. Exact text reconstruction provides a strict measure of character-level preservation, but minor transcription differences do not necessarily imply the loss of task-relevant semantics. We therefore apply the following three fixed, observation-independent questions to every observation: (1) What type of software-engineering information does this observation contain, and to which functional category does it belong? (2) What is the primary purpose of this observation in the issue-resolution process, including the object it concerns and the intended outcome? and (3) What are the main operations, results, state changes, or errors reported by this observation? The first question identifies the broad functional category, the second captures the observation’s role and objective, and the third examines its core operational semantics.
paragraphs.zh: (2) 语义问答。 精确文本重建提供了字符级保留程度的严格度量，但细微的转录差异并不一定意味着任务相关语义的丢失。 因此，我们对每条观测应用以下三个固定的、与观测内容无关的问题：(1) 该观测包含哪种类型的软件工程信息，它属于哪个功能类别？ (2) 该观测在问题解决过程中的主要目的是什么，包括它所涉及的对象和预期结果？以及 (3) 该观测报告了哪些主要操作、结果、状态变化或错误？ 第一个问题确定宽泛的功能类别，第二个问题刻画该观测的作用和目标，第三个问题考察其核心操作语义。

paragraphs.en: In the text setting , GPT-5.6-Luna answers these questions using the original textual observation. In the image setting , it answers the same questions using only the rendered image. Both settings use identical instructions and decoding configurations. GPT-6-Sol is used to compare the text-conditioned answer as the reference with the image-conditioned answer as the candidate. The judge is not informed of the corresponding input modalities and evaluates only macro-level semantic preservation. It independently assigns a score from 0 to 100 for category , purpose , and operations , where higher scores indicate stronger functional equivalence, we finally report the normalized score. We repeat each judgment 3 times and use the mean score. As shown in Fig. 2 , optical rendering preserves both textual and semantic information well under moderate compression. Fig. 1(a) shows that character accuracy remains above 95% through 4 × 4\times compression and above 90% through 6 × 6\times , but declines sharply beyond 7 × 7\times , reaching 57.67% at 10 × 10\times . For semantic preservation, Fig. 1(b) shows that the image-based representation degrades more slowly than the compression baselines and achieves the highest QA score from 4 × 4\times onward. Even at 10 × 10\times , it retains a semantic QA score of approximately 57, compared with 51 for AgentDiet, 46 for LLMLingua2, and 37 for SWE-Pruner. These results demonstrate that observation-as-image representations offer strong information preservation under moderate compression and remain more robust than text-based compression methods at higher compression factors.

paragraphs.en: To examine this form of redundancy, we conduct an oracle-style experiment on 100 sampled SWE-bench Verified tasks and compare two settings. In the Full Trace setting, the agent follows the standard workflow and retains all tool calls and observations generated during repository localization, code inspection, editing, and validation. In the Localized File Provided setting, we directly provide the code location identified during localization and omit the preceding localization trajectory. The agent then starts from the localized code and performs the remaining inspection, editing, and validation steps. Both settings use the same issue description, backbone model, execution environment, and interaction budget. This comparison examines whether the localization result can replace the verbose interaction history used to derive it.

paragraphs.en: Fig. 5 presents the overview of TraceLite and Algorithm 1 shows the detailed workflow of TraceLite. A SWE agent iteratively interacts with the repository environment through tool calls and observations. TraceLite manages the resulting interaction trace using two complementary mechanisms. First, historical optical compression preserves the most recent observations as high-fidelity text and renders an observation as a compact image once it leaves the recent window. Second, redundancy removal eliminates unnecessary information in two ways: overlap-based removal deletes content reproduced by a newer observation while preserving the latest evidence, whereas edit-triggered cleanup removes pre-edit observation payloads when the agent transitions from localization and inspection to editing and validation. Together, these mechanisms reduce the accumulated context while retaining recent evidence, historical tool calls, and repository state needed for subsequent reasoning. The entire process operates online without model training or auxiliary LLM calls.

paragraphs.en: The preliminary study shows that optical rendering can preserve most character-level and semantic information under moderate compression. This finding suggests that observations can be represented as images to reduce the context cost without training a dedicated compressor or invoking an auxiliary LLM. However, optical rendering remains an approximate representation: reducing the image resolution may obscure fine-grained details such as file paths, identifiers, line numbers, version strings, and error messages. Such errors are particularly problematic for recent observations, which usually provide the immediate evidence required to determine the agent’s next action.

paragraphs.en: Limitations of Rendering All Observations as Images. To determine whether the entire interaction trajectory can be represented visually, we compare the full-text setting with variants that render all observations as images at compression ratios of 1 × 1\times and 4 × 4\times . As shown in Table 3 , the full-text setting resolves 45 of 50 tasks (90.00%) with an average of 12.56 interaction steps. At 1 × 1\times , the success rate decreases to 74.00%, while the average number of steps increases to 17.86. This setting also consumes 65.03% more input tokens because the limited compression cannot offset the visual-token overhead and the additional exploration caused by information loss. Increasing the compression ratio to 4 × 4\times reduces this token overhead, but further lowers the success rate to 58.00% and increases the average trajectory length to 20.28 steps. Its output-token consumption is consequently 38.59% higher than that of the text setting. Overall, uniformly rendering all observations as images removes the precise recent evidence required for subsequent decisions, leading to longer trajectories and substantially lower issue-resolution performance.

paragraphs.en: Our preliminary study identifies two forms of redundancy in SWE-agent trajectories. First, observations produced at different steps may contain substantial textual overlap. paragraphs.en: Our primary benchmark is SWE-bench Verified ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) , which contains 500 human-validated issues from real-world Python repositories. Given an issue description and repository snapshot, the agent must identify the cause, modify the relevant files, and produce a patch that passes the benchmark tests. We further evaluate generalizability on DeepSWE ( Huang et al., 2026 ) , which contains original, long-horizon engineering tasks with hidden reference solutions and verifiers. This complementary setting examines whether TraceLite generalizes beyond public GitHub issues to more complex engineering workflows.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的主要基准是 SWE-bench Verified（Jimenez et al., 2024），其中包含 500 个经人工验证的、来自真实世界 Python 仓库的问题。 给定一个问题描述和仓库快照，智能体必须找出原因、修改相关文件，并生成一个能通过基准测试的补丁。 我们进一步在 DeepSWE（Huang et al., 2026）上评估泛化能力，该基准包含原创的、长周期的工程任务，并带有隐藏的参考解决方案和验证器。 这一补充设置考察的是 TraceLite 能否超越公开的 GitHub 问题，泛化到更复杂的工程工作流程。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate each method using the following metrics: (1) Resolved Rate , measured by the number and percentage of tasks whose generated patches pass all benchmark tests; (2) Steps , measured by the average number of agent–environment interaction steps per task; (3) Input Tokens and Output Tokens , measured by the average cumulative token consumption per task; (4) Cost ($/task) , calculated from the input and output tokens consumed by the coding agent and any auxiliary API models. To enable comparisons across settings, we additionally normalize the cost against the corresponding Vanilla full-trace baseline, whose normalized cost is set to 1; and (5) Compression Overhead , evaluated in terms of offline training resources, online processing latency per observation, and auxiliary-model token consumption. Token and cost changes are reported relative to the full-trace baseline.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用以下指标评估每种方法：(1) 解决率（Resolved Rate），以生成的补丁通过全部基准测试的任务数量和百分比来衡量；(2) 步数（Steps），以每个任务的平均智能体–环境交互步数来衡量；(3) 输入令牌（Input Tokens）与输出令牌（Output Tokens），以每个任务的平均累计令牌消耗量来衡量；(4) 成本（$/task，美元/任务），由编码智能体及任何辅助 API 模型所消耗的输入和输出令牌计算得出。 为了在不同设置之间实现可比性，我们还将成本相对于对应的 Vanilla 全轨迹基线进行归一化，该基线的归一化成本设为 1；以及 (5) 压缩开销（Compression Overhead），从离线训练资源、每个观测的在线处理延迟以及辅助模型的令牌消耗等方面进行评估。 令牌和成本的变化均相对于全轨迹基线进行报告。

paragraphs.en: Statistical Analysis. Since all methods are evaluated on the same benchmark instances, we conduct paired two-sided tests between TraceLite and each baseline. We use the exact McNemar test for Resolved Rate and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for Steps , Input Tokens , Output Tokens , and Cost ($/task) . Differences with p < 0.05 p<0.05 are considered statistically significant.
paragraphs.zh: 统计分析。 由于所有方法都在相同的基准实例上评估，我们在 TraceLite 与每个基线之间进行配对双侧检验。 我们对解决率使用精确 McNemar 检验，对步骤数、输入令牌数、输出令牌数和成本（$/任务）使用 Wilcoxon 符号秩检验。 p < 0.05 p<0.05 的差异被认为具有统计显著性。

paragraphs.en: Vanilla (Full Trace) retains every tool call and observation as raw text throughout the task without performing any compression.
paragraphs.zh: Vanilla（完整轨迹，Full Trace）在整个任务过程中将每一次工具调用和观察结果都保留为原始文本，不进行任何压缩。

paragraphs.en: RAG indexes historical observations and retrieves the most relevant chunks according to the agent’s current information need.
paragraphs.zh: RAG 对历史观察进行索引，并根据智能体当前的信息需求检索最相关的分块。

paragraphs.en: LLMLingua2 ( Pan et al., 2024 ) formulates prompt compression as token classification and uses a separately trained encoder to remove less informative tokens.
paragraphs.zh: LLMLingua2（Pan et al., 2024）将提示压缩表述为词元分类任务，并使用单独训练的编码器来移除信息量较低的词元。

paragraphs.en: LongCodeZip ( Shi et al., 2025 ) applies a two-stage code compression strategy that ranks function-level chunks using conditional perplexity and selects relevant code under a token budget.
paragraphs.zh: LongCodeZip（Shi et al., 2025）采用了一种两阶段代码压缩策略，该策略使用条件困惑度对函数级别的代码块进行排序，并在 token 预算内选择相关代码。

paragraphs.en: SWE-Pruner ( Wang et al., 2026 ) employs a trained neural skimmer to perform task-aware, line-level pruning according to the agent’s current information need.
paragraphs.zh: SWE-Pruner（Wang et al., 2026）采用训练好的神经略读器，根据智能体当前的信息需求执行任务感知的行级剪枝。

paragraphs.en: SeeRepo ( Ma et al., 2026a ) constructs a repository graph over files, classes, and functions to provide structurally relevant repository context for agent reasoning.
paragraphs.zh: SeeRepo (Ma et al., 2026a) 在文件、类和函数之上构建仓库图，为智能体推理提供结构相关的仓库上下文。

paragraphs.en: AgentDiet ( Xiao et al., 2026 ) uses an auxiliary reflection LLM to identify and remove redundant, unhelpful, or expired information from the interaction history.
paragraphs.zh: AgentDiet (Xiao et al., 2026) 使用一个辅助反思 LLM 来识别并移除交互历史中冗余、无用或过期的信息。

paragraphs.en: We use GPT-5.6-Luna ( OpenAI, 2026b ) and Gemini-3.8-Flash ( Google DeepMind, 2026 ) as the backbone models. For SWE-bench Verified, we set the reasoning effort to high , the temperature to 0, and the maximum number of interaction steps to 250. We randomly partition its 500 tasks into two disjoint subsets: 100 tasks are used exclusively for the parameter study in Section 5.4 , while the remaining 400 tasks are used for the main evaluation. Based on the parameter study, we set the recent-text window size to three observations and the image compression ratio to 4 × 4\times for all subsequent experiments. We use GPT-5.6-Luna for the main evaluation and Gemini-3.8-Flash to examine the generalizability of TraceLite across model families. For DeepSWE ( Huang et al., 2026 ) , we use GPT-5.6-Luna with xhigh reasoning effort, as described in Section 5.5 . Because DeepSWE is a long-horizon benchmark that may require substantially more interactions, we impose no maximum step limit. All methods are implemented within mini-SWE-agent, a lightweight software engineering agent framework that provides tools for repository search, file inspection and editing, test execution, and shell interaction. For each benchmark, all methods use the same agent prompt, tool set, execution environment, reasoning configuration, and interaction budget.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用 GPT-5.6-Luna（ OpenAI, 2026b ）和 Gemini-3.8-Flash（ Google DeepMind, 2026 ）作为骨干模型。 对于 SWE-bench Verified，我们将推理力度设置为 high，温度设置为 0，最大交互步数设置为 250。 我们将其 500 个任务随机划分为两个不相交的子集：100 个任务专门用于第 5.4 节的参数研究，其余 400 个任务用于主要评估。 基于参数研究，我们在后续所有实验中将近期文本窗口大小设置为三条观测记录，图像压缩比设置为 4 × 4\times。 我们使用 GPT-5.6-Luna 进行主要评估，并使用 Gemini-3.8-Flash 检验 TraceLite 在不同模型家族之间的泛化能力。 对于 DeepSWE（ Huang et al., 2026 ），我们按照第 5.5 节的描述，使用推理力度为 xhigh 的 GPT-5.6-Luna。 由于 DeepSWE 是一个长时程基准，可能需要大幅更多的交互，因此我们不设置最大步数限制。 所有方法均在 mini-SWE-agent 中实现，这是一个轻量级软件工程智能体框架，提供仓库搜索、文件查看与编辑、测试执行以及 shell 交互等工具。 对于每个基准，所有方法均使用相同的智能体提示词、工具集、执行环境、推理配置和交互预算。

paragraphs.en: For the baseline implementations, RAG uses UniXCoder ( Guo et al., 2022 ) to encode queries and historical observations and retrieves the top eight most relevant chunks. LongCodeZip uses Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct ( Hui et al., 2024 ) to estimate conditional perplexity and rank code chunks for compression. SWE-Pruner employs Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) as its neural skimmer to estimate the task relevance of individual code lines. AgentDiet ( Xiao et al., 2026 ) uses GPT-5-mini as the auxiliary reflection model for identifying redundant, unhelpful, or expired information in the interaction history. We use the same target compression ratio for every observation across all compression baselines to ensure a controlled comparison.

paragraphs.en: We conduct the main experiment on SWE-bench Verified using GPT-5.6-Luna as the backbone model within the mini-SWE-agent framework. We evaluate whether each method can reduce context consumption while preserving the agent’s ability to resolve real-world software issues.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在 mini-SWE-agent 框架内，使用 GPT-5.6-Luna 作为主干模型，在 SWE-bench Verified 上开展了主要实验。 我们评估每种方法能否在保留智能体解决真实世界软件问题能力的同时，降低上下文消耗。

paragraphs.en: Issue-Resolution Performance. As shown in Table 4 , TraceLite achieves the numerically highest resolved rate, resolving 313 of 400 tasks (78.25%). Its performance is statistically comparable to the full-trace baseline (78.00%, p = 1.000 p=1.000 ), AgentDiet (77.75%, p = 0.8679 p=0.8679 ), and RAG (76.25%, p = 0.2799 p=0.2799 ), indicating that compression does not reduce issue-resolution capability. In contrast, SWE-Pruner, LLMLingua2, LongCodeZip, and SeeRepo achieve significantly lower resolved rates than TraceLite ( p < 0.05 p<0.05 ). LongCodeZip, for example, reduces input tokens by 55.08% but lowers the resolved rate to 64.50% ( p = 2.38 × 10 − 11 p=2.38\times 10^{-11} ). These results show that minimizing tokens alone is insufficient, an effective method must preserve the information required for subsequent decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 问题解决性能。 如表4所示，TraceLite取得了数值上最高的问题解决率，在400个任务中解决了313个（78.25%）。 其性能与完整轨迹基线（78.00%，p = 1.000 p=1.000）、AgentDiet（77.75%，p = 0.8679 p=0.8679）以及RAG（76.25%，p = 0.2799 p=0.2799）在统计上相当，表明压缩并不会降低问题解决能力。 相比之下，SWE-Pruner、LLMLingua2、LongCodeZip和SeeRepo的问题解决率显著低于TraceLite（p < 0.05 p<0.05）。 例如，LongCodeZip将输入token减少了55.08%，但问题解决率降至64.50%（p = 2.38 × 10 − 11 p=2.38\times 10^{-11}）。 这些结果表明，仅仅最小化token是不够的，一种有效的方法必须保留后续决策所需的信息。

For offline cost, we report the training time and computational resources required by each method. We additionally report the input and output tokens consumed by separately invoked auxiliary API models. A dash indicates that the corresponding cost is not applicable or that the method does not invoke an auxiliary API model.

paragraphs.en: We conduct an ablation study on 100 tasks randomly sampled from the 400-task evaluation split of SWE-bench Verified. These tasks are disjoint from the 100-task development split used for the parameter study in Section 5.4 . The ablation study examines the contributions of the three components of TraceLite: historical optical compression, overlap-based removal, and edit-triggered history cleanup. We evaluate all eight combinations of the three components, including each component individually, their pairwise combinations, and the complete configuration. Full-history prompting without any compression component serves as the reference configuration.

paragraphs.en: As shown in Table 7 , retaining only the most recent observation substantially reduces input-token consumption, but decreases the pass rate from 83.67% to 81.63% and increases the average number of interaction steps from 14.63 to 20.71. Retaining two recent observations recovers the full-history pass rate, although the agent still requires more steps. The three-step window achieves the highest pass rate of 85.71% while consuming 152,155 input tokens, representing a 44.76% reduction relative to the full-history baseline. It also reduces average output-token consumption from 7,576 to 6,958.

paragraphs.en: As shown in Table 8 , the 1 × 1\times setting increases input token cost by 41.45%, indicating that the reduction in image resolution is insufficient to offset the resulting visual-token overhead. paragraphs.en: Generalization across Benchmarks. We further evaluate TraceLite on DeepSWE ( Huang et al., 2026 ) using GPT-5.6-Luna with xhigh reasoning effort and no maximum interaction-step limit. We retain the same agent framework and default compression parameters to examine whether TraceLite generalizes beyond SWE-bench Verified. As shown in Table 10 , TraceLite preserves the 60.00% resolved rate of the full-trace baseline while reducing input tokens, output tokens, and normalized cost by 50.99%, 6.77%, and 44.31%, respectively. Despite requiring slightly more interaction steps (94.79 versus 89.34), it achieves the lowest input-token consumption and cost among all methods. LongCodeZip obtains the second-lowest cost but resolves one fewer task and increases output-token consumption by 27.06%. AgentDiet achieves the highest resolved rate of 62.00%, but its auxiliary GPT-5-mini calls increase its normalized cost to 1.6403. paragraphs.en: (1) Generalization Across Agent Frameworks. Due to the computational and API costs of evaluating complete trajectories, we conduct experiments only with mini-SWE-agent, which may limit generalization to other agent frameworks. Nevertheless, mini-SWE-agent is a competitive framework whose iterative workflow of repository search, file inspection, editing, and testing is representative of modern coding agents. Moreover, TraceLite processes tool calls and observations without relying on framework-specific prompts or architectures. Evaluations across multiple backbone models and benchmarks further mitigate this threat. (2) Data Leakage and Benchmark Contamination. Because SWE-bench Verified contains public GitHub issues and patches, its solutions may occur in model pretraining data and inflate absolute resolved rates. We mitigate this threat by additionally evaluating on DeepSWE ( Huang et al., 2026 ) , whose tasks are written from scratch and whose solutions and verifier tests remain hidden from the agent. For SWE-bench Verified, we follow the official protocol without exposing gold patches or evaluation results. Since all methods use identical models and instances, contamination is unlikely to systematically favor TraceLite, although its influence cannot be completely eliminated. (3) Correctness of Patches. Both benchmarks assess patches using executable tests or program-based verifiers, which cannot guarantee correctness for every possible input. DeepSWE reduces this risk using hand-written functional verifiers that evaluate observable behavior and accept alternative implementations; its independent audit reports only 1.4% disagreement between the verifier and an LLM judge ( Huang et al., 2026 ) . Because all methods are evaluated with the same verifiers, potential imperfections may affect absolute pass rates but are unlikely to alter their relative comparison.

paragraphs.en: LLM-Based Issue Resolution . LLM-based agents have been widely applied to repository-level issue resolution. SWE-agent ( Yang et al., 2024 ) enables models to iteratively inspect repositories, modify code, and validate patches, while AutoCodeRover ( Zhang et al., 2024 ) incorporates structure-aware code search and Agentless ( Xia et al., 2025 ) decomposes resolution into localization, repair, and validation. Subsequent work improves issue localization through graph-guided reasoning ( Liu et al., 2026b ) , tool-interactive training ( Ma et al., 2026b ) , and test-driven execution ( Liu et al., 2026a ) , or enhances resolution through ensemble reasoning ( Tian et al., 2026 ) and turn-control strategies ( Gao and Peng, 2026 ) . Meng et al. ( Meng et al., 2026 ) further examine the capabilities and limitations of current bug-fixing agents. Unlike these studies, TraceLite focuses on compressing growing interaction traces and is complementary to advances in agent reasoning and issue resolution.

paragraphs.en: Token Compression for LLM Agents . Existing approaches include general-purpose and coding-specific methods. LLMLingua2 ( Pan et al., 2024 ) performs general prompt compression using a trained token classifier. For coding agents, AgentDiet ( Xiao et al., 2026 ) invokes a reflection LLM to remove redundant or expired trajectory content, while LongCodeZip ( Shi et al., 2025 ) uses conditional perplexity for function- and block-level code pruning. SWE-Pruner ( Wang et al., 2026 ) employs a trained neural skimmer for line-level pruning. These code-oriented methods do not directly handle heterogeneous tool observations. SeeRepo ( Ma et al., 2026a ) improves navigation through visual repository graphs but augments rather than compresses interaction histories. TraceLite combines optical compression with overlap-based removal and edit-triggered cleanup, requiring neither model training nor auxiliary model calls.

paragraphs.en: Coding Agents and Context Management . Coding agents solve software engineering tasks through iterative reasoning, tool use, and environment feedback. SWE-agent ( Yang et al., 2024 ) manages context using windowed file views and observation removal, whereas mini-SWE-agent ( Yang et al., 2024 ) maintains a simple append-only interaction history. OpenHands ( Wang et al., 2024 ) provides context condensers that summarize earlier interactions. Commercial and open-source agents adopt similar mechanisms: Claude Code ( Anthropic, 2026 ) , Codex ( OpenAI, 2026a ) , TRAE ( Gao et al., 2025 ) , and OpenCode ( OpenCode, 2026 ) compact or summarize historical context during long-running tasks. These approaches may discard fine-grained information or require additional model inference. In contrast, TraceLite retains recent observations as text and compresses historical context through optical re-encoding and deterministic redundancy removal.

paragraphs.en: We present TraceLite, a training-free framework that compresses SWE-agent traces through recent-text preservation, historical optical compression, and redundancy removal. Evaluations across two benchmarks and backbone models demonstrate its generalizability. On SWE-bench Verified, TraceLite achieves a 78.25% resolved rate while reducing input tokens and API cost by 33.05% and 21.30%, respectively, with only 0.438 seconds of latency per observation. These results demonstrate that TraceLite improves SWE-agent efficiency without offline training, auxiliary LLM calls, or degraded issue-resolution capability.
